meta.titre: Hitler and the Treaty of Versailles: terms, breaches and the road to 1939
meta.sous_theme: The terms of Versailles and Hitler's steps to the Second World War

sections.contenu_markdown: The treaty signed in 1919 at the palace of Versailles near Paris took the German colony of Kamerun, so its effects reached our own country. Many Germans hated the treaty, and in the 1930s a new leader promised to destroy it. Each breach made the next step easier, until war broke out in 1939. Examiners ask for the provisions of the treaty and the steps taken against it, often in the same question. This course gives you both lists and the way to link them.

items: The First World War, 1914 to 1918, was won by Britain, France and their allies.
Germany was ruled by Adolf Hitler from 1933.
Appeasement means giving way to demands in order to avoid war.

sections.titre: The Treaty of Versailles and the steps taken against it
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The treaty of 28 June 1919

Germany was not allowed to negotiate; Germans called it a diktat, a dictated peace.

| Area | Provision |
|---|---|
| Blame | Germany accepted guilt for the war (war guilt clause) |
| Reparations | Germany had to pay compensation |
| Land | Alsace-Lorraine returned to France; a Polish Corridor created; Danzig made a free city; the Saar placed under League control for fifteen years |
| Colonies | Germany lost all colonies, which became mandates, including Kamerun |
| Army | Limited to 100,000 men, no conscription, no tanks, no air force, a small navy |
| Rhineland | Left demilitarised |
| Union with Austria | Forbidden |
| League | The League of Nations was created |

### Hitler's steps

| Year | Step |
|---|---|
| 1933 | Hitler became Chancellor and withdrew from the Disarmament Conference and the League |
| 1935 | The Saar voted to return to Germany; Hitler announced conscription and an air force; Britain signed a naval agreement with Germany |
| 1936 | German troops entered the Rhineland |
| 1938 | Union with Austria (Anschluss); the Sudetenland was handed over after the Munich Agreement |
| 1939 | Germany occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia in March and invaded Poland on 1 September; Britain and France declared war on 3 September |

### Why Hitler could do it

Many people in Britain thought the treaty was too harsh, Britain and France wished to avoid another war, and the League was weak. This policy of appeasement encouraged him until Poland.

variantes.contenu_markdown: Write Adolf Hitler, Chancellor of Germany from 1933. Do not write Mussolini or Chamberlain, who were other leaders.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the main terms
variantes.contenu_markdown: Group terms as blame, money, land, colonies, army and Rhineland. Give at least four with a short detail each.

variantes.nom: Describe the steps and link to war
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how breaches led to the Second World War
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write steps in date order. After each step add one link such as: this showed that Britain and France would not act, so Hitler went further. Finish with Poland in 1939.

sections.enonce_markdown: Describe the terms of the Treaty of Versailles that limited the German armed forces and explain how Hitler broke them. [8 marks]

etapes.justification: There is one part about terms and one about breaches.

etapes.resultat_markdown: Army of 100,000, no conscription, no tanks, no air force, small navy, Rhineland demilitarised.
1935 conscription and air force; 1935 naval agreement with Britain; 1936 troops in the Rhineland.
Britain and France did not use force and many thought the treaty harsh.

etapes.justification: A summary sentence completes the answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Each breach went unpunished and encouraged more.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The Treaty of Versailles limited the German army to 100,000 men, forbade conscription, tanks and an air force, allowed only a small navy and demilitarised the Rhineland. Hitler broke these terms step by step. In 1935 he announced conscription and an air force, and Britain signed a naval agreement with Germany. In 1936 German troops entered the Rhineland. Britain and France did not use force because many people thought the treaty harsh and they wished to avoid another war. Each unpunished breach encouraged Hitler to go further.

items.erreur_markdown: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1945.
items.pourquoi_faux: It was signed in 1919 after the First World War.
Germany lost all of them as mandates.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Kamerun and other colonies became mandates.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing up the Sudetenland and the Rhineland.
items.pourquoi_faux: The Rhineland was on the Franco-German border and the Sudetenland was in Czechoslovakia.
The question also asks for Hitler's steps.
items.correction_markdown: Write both parts and link them to the outbreak of war.

items.enonce_markdown: State three terms of the Treaty of Versailles that limited the German armed forces.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each correct term. For example: **an army of 100,000, no conscription, no tanks or air force, a small navy, a demilitarised Rhineland.**

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why German troops entering the Rhineland in 1936 broke the treaty and why Britain and France did not use force.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for both parts. The Rhineland was to be demilitarised. Britain and France did not want another war, many thought the treaty harsh, and the League was weak. **This was a breach met by appeasement.**

items.enonce_markdown: Describe the steps Hitler took between 1933 and 1939 against the treaty and explain how they led to war. [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for dates and links: 1933 League and Disarmament Conference left; 1935 Saar, conscription, air force, naval agreement; 1936 Rhineland; 1938 Anschluss and Sudetenland; 1939 Czechoslovakia and Poland. **Britain and France declared war on 3 September 1939.**

items_markdown: Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919; Germany lost land and all colonies.
Army limited to 100,000, no conscription, no tanks or air force, Rhineland demilitarised.
Germany accepted guilt and paid reparations.
Hitler's steps: 1933 leave League; 1935 conscription and Saar; 1936 Rhineland; 1938 Anschluss and Sudetenland; 1939 Poland.
Appeasement and the weakness of the League helped Hitler.
Always answer both parts: the treaty and the steps.
